name: VA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by about 22 points on partisan baseline
Griffith holds a roughly 20-to-1 fundraising advantage with $974K on hand
Challenger Powers raised only $85K with no outside support
Markets price the Democratic win chance near 3%
model.rationale: A 22-point Republican district, a well-funded incumbent, and a challenger with minimal resources leave Democrats with no clear path; even a favorable national environment moves this only a few points. Markets and structural fundamentals align on a comfortable Griffith win.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Griffith or a dramatic fundraising reversal could tighten the race, but no current evidence suggests either will materialize.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Virginia's 9th District in the southwest part of the state leans Republican by roughly 22 points. Morgan Griffith, the Republican incumbent, secured renomination and is seeking another term. He enters the general election with a commanding financial position, having raised about $1.8 million and holding nearly $1 million in cash on hand.

Democrat Joy Powers has raised about $85,000, with roughly $14,000 remaining, and no outside spending has been reported on either side. No public polls or expert ratings follow the race, and prediction markets give Democrats about a 3 percent chance of winning. The national environment leans Democratic this cycle, but that shift falls far short of what would be needed to overcome the district's strong Republican tilt. Griffith is expected to win comfortably.
